data.turoyo: W u=šarṭ di=šahada di=ṭayuṯayḏan aḥna hiya haṯe yo. W gdəmmutle ḥamšo=šarṭat ne, w gəmšahdutu, w i=naqlayo ktowutu ṭaye.
data.translation: Das Glaubensbekenntnis zu unserer islamischen Religion, das ist hier Bedingung bei uns. Ihr müßt es sprechen, es sind fünf Vorschriften, ihr müßt das Glaubensbekenntnis sprechen, und dann seid ihr Muslime."

rationale: Sparse II Infectum cell; prospective second-person plural instruction differs from inherited dependent third-person requirement.

data.turoyo: Aḥ=ḥawronayḏi mu=gabano w m-ano diḏi, ma=tre gabe, kul=ḥa mšahadle lu=goran du=dinayḏe. <...>
data.translation: Meine Gefährten auf dieser und auf jener Seite von mir, auf beiden Seiten, legten alle das islamische Glaubensbekenntnis ab gemäß ihrer Religion. <...>

rationale: Sparse II Preterit cell; affirmative distributive performance complements the inherited negated first-person form.

data.translation: <...> Ich antwortete: "Was für ein Glaubensbekenntnis soll ich denn ablegen, was soll ich denn sagen?" <...>

rationale: Sparse II Infectum cell; first-person deliberative question. It occurs in an existing Imperativ context but lacks its own Infectum filing.

data.turoyo: <...> w maq=qaḥrayḏi ḥəngi d ʕaǧəz mini ʕal d lo=komšahadno lo=koweno ṭayo xtoṯe, mədle li=mḥato w xrizole l ṣawʕe, ʕamuqo, w naqla admo komo nafəq.
data.translation: <...> Und aus lauter Wut über mich, weil er sich so ärgerte, daß ich kein Glaubensbekenntnis ablegte und nicht Muslime wurde wie er, ergriff er die Nadel und stieß sie sich tief in den Daumen. Es quoll schwarzes Blut hervor.

rationale: Sparse II Infectum cell; negative ko- form and explicit religious context.

summary: Extract JL 18.7.7 from the translation into refs
before: They approached me and said: “Testify” – I replied: “What should I testify? What should I say?” – They said: “Aren’t you a Muslim?” – I said: “No” JL 18.7.7;
after: They approached me and said: “Testify” – I replied: “What should I testify? What should I say?” – They said: “Aren’t you a Muslim?” – I said: “No”
rationale: The reference has been swallowed by the translation and refs is empty. JL 18.7/7 contains the quoted exchange, including the answer No, so the reference can be moved to refs without changing the translated wording.

summary: New idiom: ašhadu billah 'ich bezeuge bei Gott' (arabisches Zitat)

data.headword: ašhadu billah 'ich bezeuge bei Gott' (arabisches Zitat)
data.turoyo: U šer omər: “Ašhadu billah hawxa yo.”
data.translation: Der Löwe sprach: »Ich bezeuge bei Gott, so ist es!«

rationale: Permitted case-insensitive lookup search ašhadu returned no hits; retain the Arabic testimony formula as a quotation, without deriving a native Turoyo first-person form from ašhadu.

summary: II lexicalises profession of the Islamic creed without an expressed creed object. Bare mšahəd after kolozəm, prospective gəmšahdutu and deliberative mə=mšahadno retain one religious sense.
At JL 18.7/7 interrogative mə= means 'what'; it is not a negator. At /11 separate lo explicitly negates mšahadli. Neither nonperformance nor German refusal phrasing requires a new sense.
Added JL 18.7/7 Infectum illustrates a different box from the inherited Imperativ quotation; the identical command itself is not repeated as another example.
Arabic Ašhadu billah is a quoted testimony formula; it does not establish a Turoyo I first-person conjugation. A permitted search found no existing ašhadu collocation.

Permitted shḏ lookup confirms a separate MEA-derived testimony entry. PrS 85/40 reproduces the fox context already filed under šhd with prs 249/24 but spells ksohəḏ; preserve the source difference for review.
Is PrS 85/40 the passage cited as prs 249/24, and should its s/ḏ form be indexed under shḏ while retaining the existing šhd record?
Is Arabic ašhadu billah used as an integrated fixed quotation or a code switch? It is not evidence for a productive native paradigm.
Should the embedded Arabic religious formula and native II profession verb be cross-referenced explicitly after editorial review?
